newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian inflation seen at nine pct in first quarter.
newsitem.headline: Indian inflation seen at nine pct in first quarter.

text.p: Indian inflation is expected to rise to nine percent in the first quarter, fuelled by increasing money supply and an expected hike in the price of petroleum products, analysts said on Sunday.

"Inflation will rise until March-April and touch nine percent if we take into account the likely hike in petroleum prices," Aashish Pitale, an analyst with ICICI Securities and Finance Company Ltd (I-Sec), told Reuters.

Year-on-year inflation, measured by the wholesale price index, stood at 7.75 percent, a 58-week high, on January 4, compared to 7.65 percent the previous week and 5.21 percent a year earlier, the Industry Ministry said.
Pitale said the easing of monetary policy by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the increase in prices of petroleum products in July had caused the recent rise in inflation.
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's government raised prices of petroleum products by an average of about 15 percent last July.

The RBI slashed banks' cash reserve requirement to 10 percent on January 18 from 14 percent in April 1996 to make more money available to domestic industry, which has persistently complained of a tight money situation.
Analysts said the reduction in reserve requirements has released more than 250 billion rupees, which has had an expansionary impact on money supply.
"The government has to increase prices of petroleum products to reduce the rising cost of oil subsidies," said an analyst with a foreign investment firm, who asked not to be named.
A rise in petroleum product prices would push up production and freight costs, stoking inflation, analysts said.
"If oil prices are raised, inflation would touch nine percent," D.H. Pai Panandikar, an economist and corporate policy adviser, said.

Petroleum Ministry officials have said prices must be raised to bridge a rising deficit in the oil pool account, which is the subsidy the government pays India's oil firms for selling petroleum products to consumers below world prices.
But Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's ruling centre-left coalition has so far refrained from raising prices, under pressure from its communist allies.
Deve Gowda said earlier this week the government might resort to borrowing to plug the oil pool account deficit.

Local news agencies quoted Finance Minister P. Chidambaram on Friday as saying that inflation would be pushed up even if the government refrained from raising prices and met the oil pool shortfall through deficit financing.
Analysts said the inflation rate would come down in the second half of the year on expectations of record agricultural output, which will ease the supply situation in the economy.
Panandikar said many sectors such as cement, steel, aluminium and copper had built up stocks of their products and that the large supplies should also have an easing effect on inflation.
